question.text: Vindhya Ventures (Cat I VC AIF) invests INR 15 crore in startup Gupta Tech at a post-money valuation of INR 75 crore. What is Vindhya's ownership stake and Gupta's pre-money valuation?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Pre-money = Post-money - New Investment = 75 - 15 = INR 60 crore. Vindhya's stake = New Investment / Post-money = 15 / 75 = 20%. This matches the PDF 11.8.2 example logic. **The Trap:** 25% divides by pre-money instead of post-money (wrong denominator); 20%/75 crore confuses pre and post; 15% uses arbitrary math. The rule: stake = investment / POST-money; pre-money = post-money - investment. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests identical valuation-round math. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) does not cover VC. XV tests cap-table dilution with option pool adjustments which are common in term sheet drafting. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In Cat I VC term sheets, clarify whether the option pool is carved out PRE-money (founders dilute) or POST-money (everyone dilutes). A 10% option pool shuffle can materially alter the effective pre-money you're paying.
